### Also covered by

Mac Lane, *Categories for the Working Mathematician*, 2nd ed., §IV.1, book p. 79 (PDF p. 88) — item `maclane:IV.1:construction1`. The free vector space on a set is the motivating example that opens the adjunction chapter.

New aspect added by §IV.1: the same content is presented in **adjunction** rather than universal-arrow form — the bijection between linear maps out of the free space and functions into the underlying set, with naturality asserted in **both** variables (the set and the target space), each verified separately. The universal-arrow form this issue already asks for yields the adjunction through `Theory/Universal/Arrow.v:214` (`AdjunctionFromUniversalArrows`), so the increment is to state and prove the two naturality clauses and to expose the result as an `Adjunction` term, not only as a family of universal arrows.

### Also covered by

Mac Lane, *Categories for the Working Mathematician*, 2nd ed., §IV.1, book p. 80 (PDF p. 89) — item `maclane:IV.1:construction3`. The currying bijection reappears as the second motivating example of the adjunction chapter.

New aspects added by §IV.1, both of which are genuinely absent in-tree and should be folded into this issue's scope:

1. **Naturality in the middle variable.** `Structure/Cartesian/Closed.v:165` (`curry_comp_l`) and `:177` (`curry_comp`) give naturality in the domain and the codomain, but no lemma states naturality of currying in the exponent variable — nothing of the shape relating `curry (f ∘ second t)` to the action of `Functor/Hom/Internal.v:40`'s `InternalHomFunctor` on `t`. `exp_respects_iso` (`Structure/Cartesian/Closed.v:209`) is not a substitute: it transports along **isomorphisms** only.
2. **The adjunction as a term.** No `Adjunction` instance witnesses (− × T) ⊣ (T ⇒ −). The four constituents exist — `exp_iso` (`Structure/Cartesian/Closed.v:51`) as the hom-setoid bijection, plus the two naturality corollaries — but they are never assembled, and the left adjoint functor (− × T) : C ⟶ C is itself not defined.

The concrete instances that already exist are `Instance/Sets/Cartesian/Closed.v:38` (`Sets_Closed`) and `Instance/Coq.v:167` (`Coq_Closed`).

### Also covered by

Mac Lane, *Categories for the Working Mathematician*, 2nd ed., §IV.2, book p. 87 (PDF p. 96) — item `maclane:IV.2:construction1`. §IV.2 opens with a table of eleven forgetful functors and their left adjoints, each unit being an insertion of generators; the rows are the same mathematical obligations already filed from §III.1, namely free modules (#309), free groups and free abelian groups (#312, #298), abelianization (#229), group rings and tensor algebras (#310), the field of quotients (#307), and metric-space completion (#308). Exactly one row — the free category on a graph — is already formalized, as `FreeForgetfulAdjunction` (`Construction/Free/Quiver.v:550`) over `UniversalArrowQuiverCat` (`:518`).

New aspects added by §IV.2:

1. Each row is asked for in **adjunction** form with its unit named, rather than as a bare universal arrow.
2. The **counit** is described concretely for the free-module row: it sends a formal combination to the actual combination, exhibiting an arbitrary module as a quotient of the free module on its own elements. No in-tree statement of that form exists for any row, and it is worth stating for whichever rows this issue delivers.

Note also that `Instance/CMon.v` — the one algebraic category in-tree — has a forgetful functor (`CMon_Forget`, `:169`) but no free left adjoint, so it is the cheapest additional row available.

### Also covered by

Mac Lane, *Categories for the Working Mathematician*, 2nd ed., §IV.2, book p. 89 (PDF p. 98), Exercise 1 — item `maclane:IV.2:ex1`.

New aspects added by §IV.2: the exterior algebra is to be exhibited as a **left adjoint** of a suitable forgetful functor (rather than only as a universal arrow), and the exercise makes a point of the forgetful functor in question being **not faithful** — the target is a category of graded anticommutative algebras, so the forgetful functor discards structure that the morphisms do not see. That non-faithfulness observation should be stated as a lemma, since it is the reason the exercise is interesting and it has no in-tree counterpart (searches for `exterior`, `Grassmann`, `wedge`, `alternating` and `anticommut` return nothing tree-wide).
